meera_sales: Tideway POC — demo tomorrow. They're seeing slow TTFT on first token (p95 ~4.9s) and intermittent 429s during our prefill step. Client bursts ~120rps during warmup. Need quick triage before the exec demo, cc @alex_h @liam_eng

alex_h: On it. Hosted or Dedicated? Also paste a sample request + route config and any logs you have.

meera_sales: Hosted. Model: rw-13b-v2-int8. Route: default-prod/tideway. Client uses prefill=true, max_tokens=512. Here's a log excerpt from the time window: 

```
[2026-03-20T15:01:09Z] req=0x8f3c shard=42 batcher: queued=18
[2026-03-20T15:01:10Z] req=0x8f3c shard=42 batcher: emitted batch_size=1 (queue_time=210ms)
[2026-03-20T15:01:10Z] req=0x9a11 handler: compute_start model=rw-13b-v2-int8
[2026-03-20T15:01:11Z] kv_cache: miss key=conv_abc123
[2026-03-20T15:01:11Z] handler: respond first_token_time=2.1s
[2026-03-20T15:01:11Z] limiter: drop_reason=queue_full -> 429
[2026-03-20T15:01:12Z] req=0x8f3c shard=42 batcher: emitted batch_size=2 (queue_time=180ms)
```

liam_eng: Two immediate suspects: (1) prefill bursts produce many short-lived conversation_ids -> low KV cache hit rate; (2) batcher sends tiny batches when queue_time exceeds threshold, so per-request overhead drives up TTFT. Need queue_time histograms, batch_size histogram, and kv_cache_hit_rate for that shard.

alex_h: Also are clients setting prefer_single=true/false? If clients force single-request paths it bypasses batching.

meera_sales: Client not setting prefer_single. Metrics snapshot during the spike: batch_size p50=3 p95=12, queue_time p95=160ms, kv_cache_hit_rate=22%, errors=mostly 429 queue_full.

ops_bot: Alert: shard-42 queue depth exceeded threshold at 2026-03-20T15:02:11Z — limiter tripped -> returning 429 to clients (metric: shard.queue_overflow=73).

liam_eng: OK. Queue_time p95 160ms explains why batcher cuts small batches (we target max_queue_time=100ms default). Small batches -> more compute per token and worse first-token latency. Fixes: (A) increase batch_window_ms for this route (20ms -> 40-50ms) to allow larger batches, (B) set min_batch_size=8 to prefer batching during warmup, (C) reduce client-side burst during demo ramp to ~25-35rps, (D) improve KV caching by ensuring consistent conversation_id or enable prefix_caching for prefill.

alex_h: For immediate demo workaround: recommend throttling client to 30rps + route changes: min_batch_size=8 and batch_window_ms=50. I'll canary a config change to default-prod/tideway. Also note: tokens used in prefill are billable — customer asked about burst pricing. For now clarify: billing counts tokens generated/consumed as normal; large warmups can increase cost so mention Dedicated/reserved if they want predictable pricing.

marta_security: Quick security note: Tideway asked about retention of prefill logs and PII handling. Hosted logs are retained 7 days by default; PII redaction applies to request/response bodies for opt-in accounts. Meera, can you collect their questionnaire and I'll draft an answer.

meera_sales: Will send the questionnaire separately to you. Back to ops — applying the canary now.

ops_bot: Deploy started: canary default-prod/tideway config batch_window_ms=50 min_batch_size=8 — job id 0a3f.

alex_h: Canary results after 10 minutes: p50 TTFT improved from 1.8s -> 1.1s, p95 improved from 4.9s -> 1.4s. 429s dropped to 0 during the canary window. Batcher metrics now: batch_size p50=8 p95=12, queue_time p95=85ms, kv_cache_hit_rate unchanged at 24%.

liam_eng: Good short-term win. For longer term: (1) add warmup job that opens persistent sessions to populate KV cache instead of bursty prefill requests, (2) enable prefix caching for prefill workloads so different convo ids can still hit shared prefixes, (3) tune shard-level limiter thresholds or scale up shard count during heavy demos.

meera_sales: I'll instruct Tideway to throttle initial ramp to 30rps and run a 2-minute warmup job. I'll also send the security questionnaire answers. Thanks all! :tada: 

alex_h: I'll roll the canary to full route and add a note to the runbook: "For prefill-heavy demos, throttle client ramp, set min_batch_size >=8 and batch_window_ms >=50ms, and prefer warmup sessions to repetitive single-use conv ids."

meera_sales: Perfect — that'll buy us the demo. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
